newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate change costs A$130 million.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate change costs A$130 million.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Australian Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman said on Tuesday that Senate amendments to a budget bill would cost about A$130 million a year.

"The cost in the first full year is A$130 million," the spokeswoman said after the Senate diluted a government plan to exclude immigrants from social security for the first two years after their arrival.
The amendments, allowing newly arrived immigrants to claim many social security entitlements but not unemployment benefits, would cost A$400 million in the first four years, she said.

Earlier, the Labor opposition estimated that the change would cost the government about a third of the budget savings in the bill, which were to be A$140 million in its first full year of operation, the fiscal year to June 1998.
The bill was part of the August 20 budget tightening, which was originally expected to save A$7.2 billion in 1997/98.

This is the first major loss from the budget, but most of the government's contentious measures have not yet been considered by the nation's upper house of parliament, called the Senate, which the government does not control.
